title: Mode 3 per-generation census (D1'-full): aligned-window engine, non-inductive pinning, LockstepPackageGen, and a timed erasure layer that makes erasure load-bearing
goal_statement: Deliver, additively, the per-generation census the lockstep design promised: a new package LockstepPackageGen whose budget fields are PackageB's {rentBound, erasure_freeze-shaped genBound, budget_le} (no cumulative exposedBound at all), a new validator-agnostic aligned-window engine window_shared_prefix (the generalisation of horizon_shared_prefix to an arbitrary window matured in both chains), a NEW non-inductive per-window pinning theorem, new lockstep headlines at confirmation depth 2n that need no shared genesis, and a timed layer (stolenAt; NoPrematureTheftLock / ErasureTimedLock phrased against rosterGen ∘ (·/n), the roster's switch grid) in which ErasureTimedLock is CONSUMED by the derivation of genBound from a pre-retirement theft-rate. Answers to the three questions asked: (1) a pure budget-transport lemma (per-generation rates + erasure ⇒ LockstepPackage.exposedBound at lagSched) is NOT achievable — exposedBound at any window is a union over all future generations j ≥ rosterGen(W−1) and per-generation rates bound each j-slice by T but not the union; a machine-checked counter-witness (n=2, T=1, rosterGen ≡ 0, Stolen i j := i = j) is included — so the safety proof must change, and it changes by a NEW engine + NEW pinning theorem + NEW headlines placed next to the old ones (nothing existing is modified). (2) 'Generalising horizon_shared_prefix' concretely means: replace the fixed pigeonhole window u := tip.slot+1−n by an arbitrary u with maturity in both chains (u+n ≤ tip.slot+1 and u+n ≤ tip'.slot+1), restrict honest-slot uniqueness to that window (HonestSlotsUniqueOn u n), and replace hkdeep by 'the block at height k sits strictly below u' — the proof is the existing one minus the slot-gap step, plus public copies of the two private helpers; 'generalising the pinning lemma' means swapping the census from exposedBound-at-lagSched (which needed the induction hypothesis to discharge the ≥ lagSched side condition, and genesis_gen for window 0) to genBound at j := the window's declared generation g, which removes the induction, the lag, and the genesis base case entirely. (3) Depth 2n IS unavoidable for the aligned-window route in the worst case (exactly n + ((tip.slot+1) mod n) ≤ 2n−1 in positions): the last aligned window matured in the lower chain starts at ((tip.slot+1)/n − 1)·n, which can be as low as tip.slot + 2 − 2n; the core theorem is stated with an explicit window W and 'B.slot < W·n' so the sharp form is available for free, and the headlines use the clean 2n. Any depth-n statement would have to consult the sliding trailing window, which straddles the unpinned tip window where the two chains may declare different generations — that is the cumulative reading (D1'-thin) or a ρ+2T/3T factor loss, not a per-generation census.

(2) The per-generation corruption predicate badLockAt n rosterGen rented Stolen s := rented s ∨ Stolen (producerForSlot n s) (rosterGen (s / n)) — the design note's 'intended consequence' predicate, chain-independent, a pure function of the slot; badLockAt_iff_or (Iff.rfl); AlignedBounded n bad := ∀ W, (badSlotsIn bad (W*n) n).card ≤ maxByzantine n; alignedBounded_of_bounded. (4) structure LockstepPackageGen (fields unforgeable, declared, hashInj, rentBound, genBound, budget_le — genBound is syntactically PackageB.erasure_freeze's expression so a PackageB field can be passed verbatim); LockstepPackageGen.alignedBudget; LockstepPackage.toGen (thin ⇒ gen when rosterGen skips no value, via erasure_freeze_of_exposedBound at u := (W+1)·n). (5) lockstep_window_declares_rosterGen — the NON-INDUCTIVE per-window pinning theorem (no hHead, no lag, no genesis_gen). (6) honestSlotsUniqueOn_lockstep — uniqueness on one aligned window matured in both chains, for badLockAt, over chainUnionRecord. (7) lockstepGen_shared_prefix (explicit window W, sharp form) and lockstepGen_shared_prefix_deep (k + 2n < length picks W := (sTip.slot+1)/n − 1). (8) Headlines (genesis-free, depth 2n): lockstepGen_recent_tip_ancestor_agreement, lockstepGen_recent_tip_ancestor_mem, lockstepGen_recent_genesis_agreement. (9) Consistency witness exposedBound_not_of_genBound (pure budget transport is impossible), optional. ~480 lines.

(4) structure LockstepPackageTimed (unforgeable at Stolen := stolenOf stolenAt, declared, hashInj, notBefore, notAfter, rentBound, preRetirementTheftBound, budget_le); LockstepPackageTimed.toGen; end-to-end lockstepTimed_recent_tip_ancestor_agreement and lockstepTimed_recent_tip_ancestor_mem. ~220 lines.

new_defs.name: HonestSlotsUniqueOn
new_defs.signature: def HonestSlotsUniqueOn (u len : Nat) (bad : ByzantineSlots) (record : SlotRecord) : Prop := ∀ s, u ≤ s → s < u + len → ¬ bad s → ∀ ⦃B B' : Block⦄, B ∈ record s → B' ∈ record s → B = B'
new_defs.meaning: Honest-slot uniqueness demanded only on the slots of one window. This is what lets the engine consume a corruption predicate that is sound only where both chains are pinned (window W at generation rosterGen W). HonestSlotsUnique bad record (Definitions.lean:498) implies it for every u, len (honestSlotsUniqueOn_of_unique).

new_defs.name: badLockAt
new_defs.signature: def badLockAt (n : Nat) (rosterGen : Nat → Nat) (rented : ByzantineSlots) (Stolen : Nat → Nat → Prop) (s : Nat) : Prop := rented s ∨ Stolen (producerForSlot n s) (rosterGen (s / n))
new_defs.meaning: The per-generation corruption predicate of LOCKSTEP_DESIGN.md:127-133 ('rented s ∨ Stolen (producerForSlot n s) (rosterGen (window s))'): a slot is bad if rented or its producer's key OF THE GENERATION THE ROSTER IS AT IN THAT GRID WINDOW is stolen. Chain-independent and un-lagged; no ∃ j ≥ … cumulative reading. Sound (for uniqueness) exactly on windows pinned in both chains — which is why it is consumed through HonestSlotsUniqueOn, not HonestSlotsUnique.

new_defs.name: AlignedBounded
new_defs.signature: def AlignedBounded (n : Nat) (bad : ByzantineSlots) : Prop := ∀ W, (badSlotsIn bad (W * n) n).card ≤ maxByzantine n
new_defs.meaning: The Byzantine budget on the fixed grid of aligned windows [W·n, W·n+n) only (the paper's 'grid window'). Weaker than ByzantineBounded (alignedBounded_of_bounded); it is the shape the aligned-window engine consumes. For badLockAt the sliding-window budget would cost R + 2T (two generations straddled) — the D1 factor 2 — while the aligned one costs R + T.

new_defs.name: LockstepPackageGen
new_defs.signature:
structure LockstepPackageGen (n : Nat) (rosterGen : Nat → Nat) {Sig sk pk : Type} (ops : SigOps Sig sk pk) (registry : KeyRegistry pk) (rented : ByzantineSlots) (Stolen : Nat → Nat → Prop) (honestSigned : Nat → Nat → Option Block) (now Δ : Nat) (G : Block) (R T : Nat) : Prop where
  unforgeable : SchedCoreUnforgeable n (fun _ => 0) ops registry rented Stolen honestSigned now Δ
  declared : ∀ ⦃i s : Nat⦄ ⦃B : Block⦄, honestSigned i s = some B → B.keyIndex = rosterGen (s / n)
  hashInj : SignedHashInjective (SignedDeclared n ops registry) G
  rentBound : ∀ u, (badSlotsIn rented u n).card ≤ R
  genBound : ∀ j : Nat, ((Finset.range n).filter (fun i => Stolen i j)).card ≤ T
  budget_le : R + T ≤ maxByzantine n
new_defs.meaning: The D1'-full package (LOCKSTEP_DESIGN H3's 'PackageC'): B1-as-behaviour (declared), the constant-0 core EUF-CMA surface (audit obstruction 3, unchanged), hash injectivity, and the budget in PER-GENERATION form — genBound is literally PackageB.erasure_freeze's expression (KeyStealingScheduleBudget.lean:337), so PackageB's field can be passed verbatim. NO exposedBound (no cumulative census, no lagSched), NO mono and NO genesis_gen (neither is consumed by the new route: the pinning theorem is non-inductive and per-window). Incomparable with LockstepPackage in general; LockstepPackage.toGen gives thin ⇒ gen when rosterGen is surjective (skips no value).

new_defs.name: NoPrematureTheftLock
new_defs.signature: def NoPrematureTheftLock (n : Nat) (rosterGen : Nat → Nat) (stolenAt : Nat → Nat → Nat → Prop) : Prop := ∀ i j r, stolenAt i j r → j ≤ rosterGen (r / n)
new_defs.meaning: A3/B3 timed, mode 3: a generation-j key can be stolen at real slot r only if the roster has already reached j in r's grid window. The 'switch time' of j is thereby the first grid window W with j ≤ rosterGen W — expressed without Nat.find so it is total even when rosterGen never reaches j. At rosterGen := id and R := n it is exactly NoPrematureTheft n stolenAt (KeyStealingScheduleTimed.lean:96), proved by noPrematureTheftLock_iff_flagship.

new_defs.name: ErasureTimedLock
new_defs.signature: def ErasureTimedLock (n : Nat) (rosterGen : Nat → Nat) (stolenAt : Nat → Nat → Nat → Prop) : Prop := ∀ i j r, stolenAt i j r → rosterGen (r / n) ≤ j
new_defs.meaning: B2 timed, mode 3: at real slot r nothing of a generation the roster has already moved past can be stolen — retired material was destroyed at the switch. At rosterGen := id, R := n it is exactly ErasureTimed n stolenAt (KeyStealingScheduleTimed.lean:102), proved by erasureTimedLock_iff_flagship. THIS field is consumed by genBound_of_preRetirementBound — erasure becomes load-bearing.

new_defs.name: preRetirementTheftProducers
new_defs.signature: noncomputable def preRetirementTheftProducers (n : Nat) (rosterGen : Nat → Nat) (stolenAt : Nat → Nat → Nat → Prop) (j : Nat) : Finset Nat := (Finset.range n).filter (fun i => ∃ r, stolenAt i j r ∧ rosterGen (r / n) ≤ j)
new_defs.meaning: The per-generation census a mode-3 deployment asserts: seats whose generation-j key is stolen at a real time at which j has not yet been retired (the 'while-live' count of §10.2). Mirror of recentTheftProducers (KeyStealingScheduleTimed.lean:149) with the generation floor replaced by the retirement ceiling. Under ErasureTimedLock it coincides with the timeless (Finset.range n).filter (fun i => stolenOf stolenAt i j).

new_defs.name: LockstepPackageTimed
new_defs.signature:
structure LockstepPackageTimed (n : Nat) (rosterGen : Nat → Nat) {Sig sk pk : Type} (ops : SigOps Sig sk pk) (registry : KeyRegistry pk) (rented : ByzantineSlots) (stolenAt : Nat → Nat → Nat → Prop) (honestSigned : Nat → Nat → Option Block) (now Δ : Nat) (G : Block) (R T : Nat) : Prop where
  unforgeable : SchedCoreUnforgeable n (fun _ => 0) ops registry rented (stolenOf stolenAt) honestSigned now Δ
  declared : ∀ ⦃i s : Nat⦄ ⦃B : Block⦄, honestSigned i s = some B → B.keyIndex = rosterGen (s / n)
  hashInj : SignedHashInjective (SignedDeclared n ops registry) G
  notBefore : NoPrematureTheftLock n rosterGen stolenAt
  notAfter : ErasureTimedLock n rosterGen stolenAt
  rentBound : ∀ u, (badSlotsIn rented u n).card ≤ R
  preRetirementTheftBound : ∀ j, (preRetirementTheftProducers n rosterGen stolenAt j).card ≤ T
  budget_le : R + T ≤ maxByzantine n
new_defs.meaning: Mode 3 with its temporal content formalized (the twin of PackageBTimed, KeyStealingScheduleTimed.lean:383): theft is time-stamped, A3 and B2 are fields, and the rate is the while-live per-generation census. notAfter is CONSUMED (toGen via genBound_of_preRetirementBound); notBefore is documentary here (consumed only by theft_in_era_lock), the exact mirror of mode 2 where A3 is consumed and erasure documentary.

alternatives_rejected.alt: Pure budget-transport lemma: per-generation rates + (timed) erasure ⇒ LockstepPackage.exposedBound at lagSched, leaving lockstep_recent_tip_ancestor_agreement as the headline.
alternatives_rejected.why: False. exposedProducersSched at lagSched over any window is the union over ALL generations j ≥ rosterGen(W−1) of the j-slices; per-generation rates bound each slice by T, not the union (counterexample n=2, T=1, Stolen i j := i=j; PackageB docstring:323-328). Timed erasure does not help: it confines each theft to its generation's live span but the union over future generations remains. Hence the safety proof must change (new engine, new pinning, new headlines) — additively.

alternatives_rejected.alt: Keep depth n by running the pigeonhole at the sliding trailing window with a per-generation predicate on each of the two straddled grid windows.
alternatives_rejected.why: The tip grid window is unmatured, so the two chains may declare different generations g ≠ g' there (each below quorum); the corruption predicate becomes chain-dependent or the census pays R + 2T (or 3T) — the D1 factor-2 wrinkle the design wanted to remove. The aligned route pays 2n depth instead of a factor in T; the owner chose D1'-full's shape (LOCKSTEP_DESIGN:214-218).

alternatives_rejected.alt: D1 option (b): a relaxed agreement engine that needs only bad-count < quorum (using quorum > 2·maxByzantine) to absorb R + 2T.
alternatives_rejected.why: Does not remove the chain-dependence of the tip window's predicate, and still counts two generations; it is a factor-recovery trick for the sliding window, orthogonal to (and weaker than) moving the pigeonhole inside the pinned region.

alternatives_rejected.alt: Generalize horizon_shared_prefix in place (add a window parameter to the existing theorem) and re-route the existing callers.

alternatives_rejected.alt: Express the switch times as an explicit function switchAt rosterGen j := Nat.find (∃ W, j ≤ rosterGen W) and state A3/B2 as j's switch time ≤ r < (j+1)'s switch time (literal 'j*R replaced by switch time').
alternatives_rejected.why: Nat.find needs an existence proof, which fails for generations the counter never reaches (bounded rosterGen); phrasing A3/B2 pointwise against rosterGen (r / n) is total, equivalent for reached generations, and reduces to the flagship at rosterGen := id, R := n (the two _iff_flagship lemmas).

alternatives_rejected.why: Muddies the 'erasure is load-bearing' claim (A3 would be equally load-bearing). The pre-retirement census (rosterGen (r/n) ≤ j) needs erasure alone, the exact mirror of mode 2 where A3 alone is consumed; notBefore stays as a documentary field consumed by theft_in_era_lock, as notAfter is in mode 2.
